title: Two independent transcription initiation codes overlap on vertebrate core promoters

items.q: What is a core promoter?
items.a: A stretch of DNA surrounding the transcription start site (TSS) that integrates regulatory inputs and recruits general transcription factors to initiate transcription.
items.info: The nature and causative relationship of the DNA sequence and chromatin signals that govern selection of most RNA polymerase II TSSs was unresolved.

items.q: Why is the maternal to zygotic transition a good system for this question?
items.a: It represents the most marked change of the transcriptome repertoire in the vertebrate life cycle, so it offers a unique opportunity to study rules of TSS selection and the hierarchy of events linking initiation with chromatin modifications.
items.info: In zebrafish, early development is a series of transcriptionally silent cell cycles run by inherited maternal gene products; zygotic genome activation starts at the tenth cell cycle (mid-blastula transition, MBT).

items.q: What are the two methods used and what is the main finding?
items.a: CAGE (cap analysis of gene expression) for TSS usage across early zebrafish development plus ChIP-seq positions of H3K4me3-marked promoter nucleosomes; the maternal to zygotic transition is a switch between two fundamentally different modes of defining transcription initiation.
items.concl: Transition from maternal to zygotic transcriptome drives a dynamic change of TSS usage and promoter shape.

items.q: What distinguishes the maternal from the zygotic initiation code?
items.a: Maternal TSS selection requires an A/T-rich motif (W-box); zygotic TSS selection is W-box independent and has broader dinucleotide enrichment patterns precisely aligned with the first downstream (+1) nucleosome.
items.concl: The two TSS-defining grammars coexist, often physically overlapping, in core promoters of constitutively expressed genes, enabling expression in both regulatory environments.

items.q: What two major promoter classes did CAGE previously define?
items.a: Sharp promoters with one predominant TSS, often with a TATA-box that determines TSS selection, and broad promoters with a wider TSS distribution, often overlapping a CpG island.
items.info: Even with reports on prevalence of known core promoter elements in human promoters, the actual mechanism of choosing TSSs in vertebrates was unknown.

items.q: What data set did they analyse?
items.a: A nucleotide-resolution map of transcription initiation in the zebrafish genome generated by CAGE across 12 stages, from the unfertilized egg to organogenesis.
items.info: Stages: unfertilized egg, fertilized egg, 64 cells, 512 cells, high, oblong, sphere/dome, dome/30% epiboly, shield, 14 somites, prim 6, prim 20 (0 to 33 hpf).

items.q: What classes of TSS dynamics came out of clustering?
items.a: Maternal-specific TSSs (pre-MBT), early or late zygotic TSSs (post-MBT), constitutively present TSSs, and TSSs peaking in the transitional stages.
items.info: Self-organizing map clustering of individual CAGE-defined TSSs (CTSSs); clustering of entire promoters gave a similar pattern.

items.q: What happens inside promoters whose overall expression does not change?
items.a: They often contain a population of TSSs with very heterogeneous relative usage during development, with maternal mRNAs initiated from different positions than zygotic transcripts within the same promoter.
items.info: Example shown is the cyclin 1 (ccni) promoter.
items.concl: Suggested distinct rules for TSS selection acting within the same promoter in the oocyte and the embryo.

items.q: How were shifting promoters defined and how many were there?
items.a: 911 shifting promoters whose CAGE signal in pre- and post-MBT stages overlapped by less than 40%.
items.info: A shifting score (max of forward and reverse cumulative-sum scores) with a 0.6 threshold was applied to all stage pairs; promoters qualifying in at least four early versus late pairs were kept.

items.q: How large is the typical TSS shift?
items.a: The shift occurred in either direction but mainly within a narrow window of up to 100 bp.
items.info: Maternal and zygotic dominant TSSs of these promoters showed antagonistic dynamics: degradation of inherited maternal transcripts and gradual activation of zygotic ones.

items.q: What sequence signal is found around the maternal dominant TSS?
items.a: A clear enrichment of T- and/or A-containing (WW) dinucleotides about 30 bp upstream of the maternal TSS, consistent with a functional TATA-like element.
items.info: Dinucleotide density was visualized after aligning the 911 shifting promoters at the maternal dominant TSS.

items.q: What sequence signal marks the zygotic TSS instead?
items.a: No TATA-like signal in the expected upstream position, but a sharp SS to WW boundary (local C/G versus A/T dinucleotide enrichment) precisely aligned about 50 bp downstream of the zygotic TSS.
items.concl: Two fundamentally different sequence signals guide initiation in the oocyte and in the embryo.

items.q: How many maternal TSSs have a canonical TATA-box?
items.a: Only a small fraction, under 10%; the majority contained other A/T-rich pentamers.
items.info: Match to a JASPAR TATA-box PWM was scanned in the region -35 to -22 bp; maternal versus zygotic difference P < 2.2 x 10^-16 (two-tailed Wilcoxon rank-sum test).

items.q: What is the W-box?
items.a: An A/T-rich motif found by de novo motif discovery with lower information content than the canonical TATA-box, but positioned equally at 30 bp upstream of the maternal TSS.
items.info: Found in 911 sequences with E value 1.1 x 10^-192; zygotic TSSs showed neither TATA-box nor W-box in the expected upstream region.
items.concl: Shift from W-box motif-dependent maternal TSS selection to W-box-independent zygotic selection.

items.q: Does the same distinction hold outside shifting promoters?
items.a: Yes. Dinucleotide analysis of all 8,369 constitutively expressed promoters showed the same W-box positioning upstream of the maternal dominant TSS and the same alignment of the zygotic TSS with the downstream SS-WW boundary.
items.info: Exclusively maternal and exclusively zygotic promoters also used the corresponding stage-specific signals.
items.concl: Complex TSS patterns in constitutive promoters are readouts of two independent grammars intertwined in the same core promoter region.

items.q: Why does W-box-dependent initiation predict a sharp TSS configuration?
items.a: Because W-box-dependent initiation imposes a fixed spacing of about 30 bp between the motif and the TSS, which constrains where initiation can occur.

items.q: How do maternal broad promoters fit this constraint?
items.a: They are not truly broad: they have a composite architecture of multiple individual relatively sharp CAGE tag clusters (TCs), each with its own W-box at the fixed approximately -30 bp position.
items.info: Maternal broad promoters were defined as interquantile width (q0.1-q0.9) greater than 20 bp, out of 1,944 maternal-specific promoters.

items.q: What shape do exclusively zygotic promoters have?
items.a: A less constrained TSS distribution, the familiar broad promoter shape, with the majority (over 70%) containing only one broad TC.
items.info: Constitutive promoters changed shape accordingly: single or multiple sharp TSS configuration in maternal stages to a broad configuration in zygotic stages.
items.concl: The maternal to zygotic TSS switch is accompanied by a global change in promoter architecture within the same region.

items.q: Which promoter was chosen for functional validation and why?
items.a: The constitutively active sf3a2 promoter, because it carries both maternal and zygotic promoter determinants and exhibits TSS shifting.
items.info: The tested region spanned 500 bp upstream to 200 bp downstream of the dominant zygotic TSS, fused via a txnipa intron splice acceptor to an mCherry reporter, with Tol2 transposon arms.

items.q: What happened to zygotic activity when all W-boxes were mutated?
items.a: Removal of all W-boxes did not influence zygotic transgene activity or zygotic TSS selection, as shown by fluorescence reporter activity and 5' RACE.
items.info: This confirms W-box-independent promoter usage in the embryo.

items.q: What is SL-CAGE?
items.a: Single-locus deep CAGE, a new method for detection and relative quantification of TSS usage at 1 bp resolution within one targeted promoter.
items.info: It combines 5'-complete cDNA generation as in CAGE with amplification of targeted cDNAs using gene-specific primers and paired-end sequencing (34 bp + 35 bp reads) of the single-locus library.

items.q: What did SL-CAGE in stable transgenic lines show?
items.a: Wild-type sf3a2 transgene TSS usage in early embryos was highly reproducible and perfectly correlated with maternal TSS usage of the endogenous sf3a2 gene and with CAGE; W-box removal severely reduced use of the associated downstream TSSs and gave an aberrant pattern (P < 0.01).
items.info: One-tailed Welch's two-sample t-test; mutant n = 4 lines, wild type n = 3 lines.
items.concl: Selection of those TSSs depends on a W-box signal in the oocyte, confirming two independent TSS selection mechanisms within a single promoter.

items.q: How was chromatin configuration assayed?
items.a: ChIP-seq for H3K4me3- and H2A.Z-containing nucleosomes at core promoters, in several developmental stages.
items.info: H3K4me3 marking of promoter nucleosomes was already known to precede gene transcription during zebrafish genome activation.

items.q: Where is the +1 nucleosome relative to each TSS?
items.a: The first downstream (+1) nucleosome is precisely positioned about 50 bp from the preferred zygotic TSS at constitutively active promoters in the zygotic (prim 6) stage, with no fixed spacing to the maternal TSS in any stage.
items.info: Alignment to the zygotic TSS was less sharp in earlier stages, including 512 cells, which precedes the onset of zygotic transcription.
items.concl: Positional interdependency between zygotic TSS and +1 nucleosome is a feature of the zygotic grammar, independent of W-box-guided maternal selection.

items.q: What finer sequence periodicity was found in nucleosome-bound DNA?
items.a: A 10 bp periodicity in AA and TT dinucleotide enrichment downstream of the zygotic TSS, previously identified as an intranucleosomal positioning signal.
items.info: Alternating WW-SS patterns downstream of the zygotic TSS provided an internucleosomal position signal (GC enrichment in internucleosomal regions).
items.concl: TSS selection in the vertebrate oocyte appears independent of inter- and intranucleosomal DNA signals.

items.q: What DNA underlies the +1 nucleosome before zygotic transcription?
items.a: In the pre-MBT (512 cells) stage, H3K4me3-marked nucleosomes occupied a CG/GC-enriched region and were centred at the peak of highest CG/GC enrichment, often directly overlapping maternal transcript TSSs.
items.info: Supports the idea that H3K4me3 initially appears at CpG islands before transcription.

items.q: And after genome activation?
items.a: In post-MBT (prim 6), the +1 nucleosome sits just downstream of the SS-WW boundary, about 50 bp from the zygotic TSS, occupying a WW-enriched region with a small local GC/CG peak at the nucleosome midpoint.
items.info: Downstream nucleosomes follow the same pattern of WW-enriched bound DNA alternating with internucleosomal SS enrichment.
items.concl: Initial nucleosome positioning changes in later stages to a final precise positioning correlated with the zygotic TSS.

items.q: Does transcription itself reposition the nucleosomes?
items.a: No. Ranking throughout-active genes by the timing of onset of zygotic transcription showed no association between activation timing and the precision of nucleosome positioning.
items.info: Argues against transcriptionally aided readjustment and for a pre-transcriptional repositioning process, in agreement with transcription-independent nucleosome positioning at human promoters.

items.q: What did the Tbp knockdown test add?
items.a: H3K4me3 ChIP-seq in Tbp morphants showed no change in overall H3K4me3 recruitment or nucleosome positioning at Tbp-dependent genes.
items.info: Shows H3K4me3-marked nucleosome positioning at these genes does not require Tbp-dependent recruitment of the initiation machinery or active transcription.

items.q: Why do the authors favour the W-box as the determinant of maternal TSS selection?
items.a: Because maternal TSSs have narrow peaks and lack a nucleosome-positioning sequence signature, and promoters with a canonical TATA-box lack precise nucleosome positioning in other systems.

items.q: Which factor do they propose mediates oocyte initiation?
items.a: The similarity of the W-box to the TATA-box suggests initiation in the oocyte may be mediated by the oocyte-enriched transcription nucleating factor Tbpl2 (also known as Tbp2).
items.info: This is a suggestion based on motif similarity; not tested directly in this paper.

items.q: What is the 'catchment area' model?
items.a: The zygotic grammar prefers the TSS at a fixed range from the precisely positioned +1 nucleosome, so the initiation complex chooses initiator-like sequences within a catchment area determined by nucleosome position.
items.info: Compatible with motif-independent TFIID recruitment via H3K4me3-TAF3 interactions.

items.q: What is the paper's headline claim about the two codes?
items.a: They show for the first time that two TSS selection grammars co-exist in close proximity or in physical overlap genome-wide and are differentially used at thousands of promoters active in both oocyte and embryo.
items.info: Earlier work had associated different grammars with different, separate promoters, and only a handful of promoters were known to switch between TATA-dependent and -independent initiation.
items.concl: Multiple layers of information in the same short sequence are part of why promoter codes have been hard to detect.

items.q: How were CAGE tags mapped and normalized?
items.a: 27 bp CAGE tags were mapped to the zebrafish Zv9/danRer7 assembly with Bowtie (default parameters, up to two mismatches, uniquely mapped reads only) and normalized to a referent power-law distribution of 10^6 tags with alpha = -1.25, giving tags per million (tpm).
items.info: An unmappable extra G at the 5' end, added by the template-free activity of reverse transcriptase, was removed. Analyses were run in R with Bioconductor packages and custom scripts.

items.q: How were CTSSs grouped into tag clusters and promoters?
items.a: CTSSs with at least 1 tpm in at least one of the 12 stages were clustered per stage with a maximum distance of 20 bp between neighbouring CTSSs; TCs across stages within 100 bp were aggregated into one promoter region.
items.info: TC boundaries were made robust by taking the 10th and 90th percentile of the cumulative CAGE signal. Only promoter regions with at least 5 tpm in at least one stage were used further.

items.q: How was expression profiling done?
items.a: CTSSs (or promoter regions) with at least 5 tpm in one stage were taken, tpm values across the 12 stages were divided by their standard deviation, and a self-organizing map distributed them across 5 x 5 = 25 expression profiles.
items.info: Done at two levels: individual CTSSs and entire promoter regions.

items.q: How are the dinucleotide density maps computed?
items.a: An occurrence matrix (sequences x positions, 1 if the dinucleotide is present) is built per dinucleotide, then smoothed by a weighted average using a two-dimensional Gaussian kernel with bandwidth 3 in both dimensions, and the densities are shown as shades of blue.
items.info: Extended Data Fig. 10 illustrates the procedure; the worked example there uses bandwidth 1 with covariance 0, while the main analyses use bandwidth 3.

items.q: How was TATA-box and de novo motif analysis performed?
items.a: A TATA-box PWM from JASPAR was used to scan -35 to -22 bp upstream of the TSS, reporting the maximal match percentage per promoter; de novo discovery ran MEME with default parameters on those 14 bp sequences, keeping motifs with E value at most 0.01.
items.info: The frequency of the top ten most abundant pentamers in the scanned region was also reported.

items.q: How were the reporter constructs made and injected?
items.a: The sf3a2 fragment was PCR amplified from AB* genomic DNA, cloned into a modified pDB896 vector (mCherry replacing the crystallin:gfp) by In-Fusion, and 1.5-2 nl of 20 ng/ul plasmid plus 15 ng/ul Tol2 transposase mRNA was injected into eggs within 10-15 min after fertilization.
items.info: 0.1% Phenol red was the injection marker; ecfp mRNA (30 ng/ul) was added as an injection control in imaging experiments. W-box mutations were introduced by site-directed mutagenesis PCR.

items.q: How was reporter activity quantified?
items.a: mCherry activity was measured at prim 20 by automated imaging, analysed in Zebrafish Miner software as pixel intensity normalized to the ECFP injection control and averaged over embryos, plus the percentage of expressing embryos among ECFP-positive ones.
items.info: Images were wrapped onto a reference embryo shape and overlaid by summing pixel intensities. 24 wild-type and 31 mutant injected embryos were compared.

items.q: How was 5' RACE performed and controlled?
items.a: With a FirstChoice RLM-RACE kit on total RNA from about 100 normal, reporter-expressing prim 6 embryos injected with wild-type or mutated construct; nested PCR products of expected size were gel-purified and sequenced.
items.info: A minus tobacco acid pyrophosphatase (TAP) sample was processed in parallel to show the products are specific to 5' ends of de-capped RNA.

items.q: How was the chromatin prepared for ChIP?
items.a: ChIP-IT Express Enzymatic kit (Active Motif) on MNase-type enzymatically sheared chromatin from about 5,000 embryos at 512 cells and about 3,000 at oblong, fixed in 1.85% formaldehyde for 20 min at room temperature.
items.info: 4 ug anti-H3K4me3 (Abcam ab8580) or anti-H2A.Z (Abcam ab4174) per reaction, plus a no-antibody control; ChIP was done in duplicate per stage, with overnight incubation at 4 C and 4 h decrosslinking at 65 C.

items.q: How were ChIP-seq libraries sequenced and analysed?
items.a: 10 ng ChIP DNA was end-repaired, adaptor-ligated, size-selected and amplified 18 cycles, then sequenced for 36 bp (or 56 bp for tbp morphants and controls) on HiSeq 2000; reads were mapped with Bowtie to Zv9/danRer7 allowing two mismatches, unique reads only.
items.info: Coverage was computed per strand with unextended reads, capped at 20 reads per identical position; minus-strand coverage was subtracted from plus-strand coverage. Peaks were called with MACS, default parameters, and nucleosome midpoints estimated from subtracted coverage within regions at FDR <= 0.01.

items.q: How was the Tbp knockdown set up and validated?
items.a: One-cell embryos were injected with beta-actin:yfp (Tbp-dependent) or ntl:yfp (Tbp-independent) reporters, then with one of two tbp morpholinos (1.7 nl, 2.5 mM) or a mismatch morpholino, and sorted by epiboly arrest plus loss of beta-actin:yfp with retention of ntl:yfp.
items.info: Embryos were kept at 28.5 C until controls reached 30% epiboly (4.7 hpf). About 1,500 non-injected, 1,500 mismatch, 1,200 tbp mo1 and 1,000 tbp mo2 morphants were used for ChIP. Tbp-dependent genes were those with log fold change <= -1.5 in a published morphant data set.

items.q: Where are the data?
items.a: High-throughput sequencing data are at the NCBI Sequence Read Archive under accessions SRA097279 and SRA104816; processed data and UCSC custom tracks are at promshift.genereg.net/zebrafish/.

items.text: The model leaves open what repositions the +1 nucleosome to its final post-MBT position if not transcription: the summary figure marks the early MBT step as 'nucleosome positioning signal / remodelling?' with question marks.
Tbpl2/Tbp2 as the factor reading the W-box in the oocyte is only inferred from motif similarity to the TATA-box; worth checking whether later work tested this directly.
Check how transferable the W-box versus nucleosome-anchored grammar framework is to other species and to non-embryonic contexts, e.g. for interpreting cavefish or adult-tissue CAGE promoter shapes.
